lines: Vik Uppal, founder and CIO of $2 billion Mavik Capital Management, argues outperformance comes from flexible mandates and patient, high-conviction bets where capital is scarce, not from scaling into a bureaucratic AUM factory.

Without rigid allocation buckets, he says, Mavik can capture 'tweener' opportunities such as middle-market restructurings and distressed commercial real estate that fall between traditional mandates and that larger, scale-driven rivals overlook as boring.
He treats sitting out poor deal flow as a key discipline, refusing forced deployment and resisting herd trades such as the current AI infrastructure boom.

Risk management, in his view, means building large buffers for unpredictable events rather than trusting initial underwriting assumptions, with investment and asset management teams combined so restructuring lessons feed future underwriting.
Alignment comes from every eligible employee investing personally in the funds and sharing incentive fees across the whole firm, which he says fosters an owner's mindset.
podcast: Capital Allocators – Inside the Institutional Investment Industry
title: Opportunistic Real Estate and Hard Asset Credit at Mavik – Vik Uppal (EP.525)
